title: Zenora rapid lab onboarding and success criteria
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This doc captures the goals, measurable success criteria, operational assumptions, and kickoff workshop agenda for the Zenora Rapid Lab — a 4-week engineering POC to validate Redwood Inference as the core LLM inference platform for Zenora's in-product summarization and search augmentation features.

Why this POC?
- Zenora needs predictable latency and cost while running a hybrid traffic mix (interactive summaries + nightly batch reranks).
- The Rapid Lab will validate model selection, routing policies, and telemetry hooks, and produce an acceptance checklist Zenora engineering can sign off on for a Dedicated or Private deployment decision.

Scope (in-scope):
- Integrate Redwood hosted API for two endpoints: summarize(text) and embed_and_rerank(query, candidates).
- End-to-end test harness: sample dataset (10k documents), 3 representative prompt templates, and synthetic user traffic profiles (interactive + batch).
- Basic RBAC and audit logging enabled for API keys used by the POC.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost, p95 latency, error rates, and quality metrics from eval prompt set.

Non-goals (out-of-scope for Rapid Lab):
- Production migration of all traffic to Redwood (only a subset of features will be tested).
- Full security review for PCI/HIPAA.
- Long-term autoscaling tuning for peak loads beyond the test profiles.

Primary success criteria (measurable / pass-fail):
1) Latency and availability
   - Interactive summarize endpoint: p95 latency <= 250ms when serving 20 concurrent interactive users (baseline traffic profile).
   - Batch rerank job: complete nightly job of 10k queries + 5 candidate reranks within a 1-hour window on Dedicated-equivalent capacity.
   - Service availability: < 1% error rate during test windows.

2) Cost and unit economics
   - Average cost per 1k input tokens for summarize endpoint < $0.65 (back-of-envelope target; updated after first run).
   - Projected monthly cost delta vs current self-hosted baseline <= +20% for similar latency.

3) Quality and regressions
   - For a fixed eval set of 250 prompt+document pairs, Rouge/rouge-like and a small human eval sample must show no more than 5% regression vs Zenora's current model baseline.

4) Observability and debugging
   - Token-level traceable request IDs exist for 100% of test requests and are visible in Redwood Console traces for correlation with Zenora logs.
   - Alert rules for token budget/exceptions and route fallbacks created and exercised in canary mode.

Acceptance tests (concrete):
- Run 3 interactive sessions per endpoint with recorded p95 and token counts; generate a post-run report with screenshots of Console dashboards and the raw metrics exported to Zenora S3 bucket.
- Run batch rerank job from Zenora CI, collect end-to-end latency, and validate that outputs match expected top-3 candidate ordering for 80% of test queries.
- Execute simulated failure: throttle primary model route and verify automatic fallback to a smaller variant with <2x latency increase and no request loss.

Telemetry and data retention requirements:
- Redwood retains token traces for 14 days for the POC. Zenora requires exports of aggregated token-cost reports daily and raw trace bundles on-demand.
- No PII will be sent for this POC; sample documents must be sanitized and marked in the dataset manifest.

Infrastructure and integration checklist:
- Zenora provides: dataset manifest (CSV), service account + key, sample prompts, and example client call site.
- Redwood provides: API keys scoped to POC, Console access for two Zenora engineers, a Dedicated-equivalent test pool, and a small S3 export hook.
- Network: if testing Private mode, coordinate VPC peering window (TBD). For hosted tests, ensure IP allowlist entries for Zenora CI.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Solutions lead: Maya Patel — POC orchestration, milestone ownership, first-line contact to Zenora eng.
- Integration engineer: Evan Brooks — setup client integration and CI-triggered batch runs.
- Observability SME: Lina Gomez — dashboard templates, alert rules, instrumentation guide.
- Zenora technical lead: Omar Riaz (Zenora) — dataset vendor, acceptance sign-off, provides feedback on quality.

Kickoff workshop agenda (90 minutes)
- 0-10m: Intros and POC objectives (Maya)
- 10-25m: Zenora architecture overview and target flows (Omar)
- 25-40m: Redwood architecture + relevant config knobs (Lina)
- 40-60m: Live integration plan and dataset walk-through (Evan + Zenora)
- 60-75m: Define measurable acceptance tests and runbook for failures (all)
- 75-90m: Next steps, owners, and scheduling of the 2-week progress checkpoint (Maya)

Risk register (top 5 risks and mitigations)
- Data sensitivity risk: if sanitized dataset is insufficient, fall back to synthetic dataset generation and run additional quality checks. Owner: Zenora.
- Model regression: baseline evaluation run early in week 1; if regression >5%, pause rollout and iterate on prompts. Owner: Maya + Omar.
- Networking/VPC delay: plan for hosted fallback tests; reserve a 3-day buffer for private peering. Owner: Evan.
- Cost overrun: implement token caps and budget alerts; predefine cutoff thresholds. Owner: Lina.
- Integration complexity with Zenora CI: create minimal reproducible CI job and keep it under 30min. Owner: Evan.

Weekly milestones (4-week plan)
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): dataset prepared, API keys exchanged, initial baseline metrics captured.
- Week 1: integration complete for summarize endpoint, first interactive load tests, baseline cost report.
- Week 2: batch rerank pipeline wired up and nightly job executed; first regression/quality report.
- Week 3: resiliency tests (fallbacks, degraded model paths), tuning of batching/cache policies.
- Week 4: final acceptance runs, build handoff notes for Dedicated/Private proposal, executive summary for Zenora stakeholders.

Deliverables
- Weekly status notes and metrics export (shared S3 path).
- Final acceptance report with: latency/cost/quality tables, runbook for production cutover, and a recommended deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with rough TCO.
- Post-mortem and next steps doc listing configuration parameters that had most impact.

Open questions / action items before kickoff (owner tags)
- Zenora to confirm sanitized sample dataset availability and cardinality (Omar).
- Decision on whether the POC should use hosted API only or include a private peering test (Maya + Zenora).
- Confirm availability of two Zenora engineers for the 90m kickoff (Maya).
- Create initial JIRA board and invite Zenora read-only viewers (Maya).

Back-of-envelope cost estimate
- Hosted test pool for small models + 100k inference tokens/day estimated at $800–$1,200 for the 4-week window (this is an early approximation; will update after initial runs).

Notes to self / workshop prep checklist (informal)
- Prepare Console demo showing token trace -> span correlation.
- Bring the canary rollback play for resilience demo.
- Export example dashboard URLs in advance and attach to Confluence.

Contacts and references:
- Slack: #solutions-zenora (create thread: rapid-lab-kickoff)
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-zenora-onboarding-849 (placeholder)
- JIRA: JIRA-ZEN-7421 (track tasks)

Next steps (immediate)
- Send this doc to Zenora and internal stakeholders; request dataset manifest and kickoff availability (Maya, today).
- Create the POC JIRA board and populate sprint with Week 1 tasks (Evan, by EOD).
- Schedule kickoff workshop — propose 2025-02-24 09:30 PT and include 90m block (Maya).

Status: DRAFT — this is a working Rapid Lab brief. Expect iterative edits after the kickoff workshop and as we capture initial run metrics.
